title: Two Couplets
author: Mirza Ghalib
text:
عشق پر زور نہیں ہے یہ وہ آتش غالبؔ
کہ لگائے نہ لگے اور بجھائے نہ بنے

دلِ ناداں تجھے ہوا کیا ہے
آخر اس درد کی دوا کیا ہے

links.label: Read and hear Ghalib on Rekhta

who: Mirza Asadullah Khan Ghalib (1797 to 1869) lived most of his life in Delhi and wrote in Urdu and Persian. He is among the most quoted poets of the ghazal tradition. The year shown is the year of his death; these couplets are older.
why: These are single couplets from two of his ghazals. In a ghazal each couplet stands on its own, and there is no documented occasion for these two. In plain sense: the first says love cannot be forced, it is a fire that will not light on command or go out on command. The second asks the foolish heart what has happened to it, and what cure this ache could have.
notice: Notice that each couplet is complete in two lines. In the first, the poet's own name appears, as is the custom in a ghazal's closing couplet. In the second, notice that the speaker talks to his own heart as if it were another person.
prompts: Have you ever tried to start or stop a feeling by will? What happened?
If you spoke to your own heart as a separate person today, what would you ask it?
